i1.title: Nursing Decade
i1.desc: Due to abuse and other issues, both my parents were absent. This worsened the medical conditions of my grandmothers on both sides, so I became their caregiver. I spent 10 years working non-stop, juggling part-time jobs and helping out since I couldn't work part-time in middle school. As a result, I became good at Italian cooking. I mainly pursued agriculture to be able to respond immediately to emergencies. However, because fertiliser costs were rising, I started studying using an old computer since middle school when the concept of remote work gradually emerged. I secured a production environment by repairing and reassembling PCs myself, accumulating skills in digital drawing and video production. Now that my caregiving duties have ended, I am finally using my time fully to resume my job hunt.

i2.desc: My seminar was designed for three years, providing various locations and projects where I learned statistics and interview techniques hands-on. For my graduation thesis, focusing on "Proof of Intellectual Decline," I interviewed a former inmate of a top-security prison in the US; this included a detailed investigation into inmates being able to watch Netflix there. I applied class skills to extracurricular activities. Post-COVID, I independently re-established relationships with TV stations, newspapers, and event companies. Since scheduling made my own appearances difficult, I did everything else I possibly could.

i3.title: Tech and Steps
i3.desc: Lacking many skills for video editing, I created homepages focused on animation as a byproduct of mastering the basics. Drawing from experiences at game and publishing companies, I expanded the VTuber archive patterns, and styled the Vspo! introduction page like a game. Aware of weak initial momentum on YouTube, I designed a site structure easily scraped by bots, publishing the source code to help sustain traction. Currently, site updates have paused, but I continue creating materials and pixel art. I've prepared PSD bases for about 60 Live2D characters, tried making rare chibi Live2D models, and continued writing novels. Organising documents remains my priority, but I advance creative activities to rest.

ch3.title: Persona
ch3.subtitle: Operating Principles
ch3.p1: Although there are many disturbing elements like abuse and caregiving, I have taken highly thorough countermeasures. Since I have younger siblings, I share and explain things as simply as possible.
ch3.p2: I am fundamentally a dry, positive person. During creation, I try hard to aim for negativity to understand it, but I am so positive that it's difficult. Also, due to circumstances mentioned later, I tend to think very theoretically and logically. It's quite convenient for explaining emotions theoretically.
ch3.p3: Part of the details of the abuse—the biggest issue—is in the separate material below, but I don't recommend reading it, as it depressed my counsellor.
ch3.p4: First, while I feel anger regarding the abuse, I don't think it's anything special. It's probably on the level of great figures like Hemingway; if the era had just been different, it would have been a common occurrence, and there's no reason to deny it.
ch3.p5: While abuse is procedurally wrong, from another perspective, none of the three normalised violence, so in the end, it wasn't a mistake. I have come to this understanding to make peace with the fact that I must not retaliate, nor ever do it to others.
ch3.p6: Another reason for detailing our meetings is that we all have different fathers, leading to slightly different tendencies. Since I am not the child of an affair, I was particularly targeted, and they both think deeply about this out of concern for me, so there are no special problems occurring.
ch3.p7: However, given the genetic premise, fragments of our parents' personalities exist within us. Since our mother's ferocity is definitely present somewhere, I hold countermeasure meetings with my siblings once a month.

l1.title: Anger Suppression System (Re-evaluation via Condition Completion)
l1.p1: Anger is a reaction that occurs "when you simulate doing the same thing yourself, and it causes a gap or surprise that you cannot accept".
l1.p2: It's like asking, "When you feel angry at someone littering, can you still maintain that same anger if you add the premise that they searched for a rubbish bin for over an hour?"
l1.p3: To an unacceptable act (initial evaluation), add multiple conditions as hypotheses, such as time constraints or a lack of judgement material.
l1.p4: By completing the conditions, you update the initial evaluation and control the reaction.
l1.p5: This process is the same method as "branch design" in creative writing. It is a reproducible processing structure, refined based on individual characteristics and environmental conditions.

l2.title: Theory of Positivity (Probability Improvement and Redesign)
l2.p1: What makes dreams come true is "analysis of elements" following precedents, "design of plans", and "thorough grasp of margins of error".
l2.p2: First, effort is meant to increase probability; it is not guaranteed to be rewarded. Therefore, I proceed without sparing effort in recovery and planning.
l2.p3: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence, and extraordinary dreams require extraordinary plans.
l2.p4: Breaking down the plan, it is currently difficult due to my career's future and resource issues, where even if I learn now, there's no clear prospect of restarting. (I occasionally write materials for current events on Note). I considered that loss to be greater, and since a shoulder injury from a workplace accident won't heal for a few years, I suspended physical labour.

ch3.p8: Like that, although I was abused, there are precedents if you look at other people or eras. If I suffered the most, it would be a point of pride. It doesn't serve as a reason to abandon my dreams, and if I can't laugh off my own past, what can I laugh off?
ch3.p9: From here on, things touch a little deeper, and since there are inevitably many dark parts, it becomes a matter of fine-tuning values and detailing plans.

story1.page_title: I Kept Caring for My Family at the Cost of My New-Grad Chance! | Akashi Isaka Archives
story1.title: I Kept Caring for My Family at the Cost of My New-Grad Chance!
story1.p2: And there goes my new-graduate hiring card. Even the informal offer I had lined up disappeared. If I sued, precedent says the ceiling would be about 500,000 yen. By caregiving, I mean I was looking after both of my grandmothers without parents around, one with severe Alzheimer's and the other with severe Parkinson's, basically from the time I was born. They were also needlessly heavy. Almost all body fat: around 60 kg, and about 80 kg when the dementia first started.
story1.p3: Well, half of it was probably on me too.
story1.p4: I have written about my past in a few articles, but my paternal grandmother was Soka Gakkai, while my maternal side was connected to Nishi Honganji and Nichiren traditions. Because my paternal grandmother saw it as the same broad lineage, she tried to recruit people. My father refused, and then his older brother lost his first wife, and the family kept coming apart in midair while she sank further into it. My paternal grandfather died before I was born. Too much alcohol and tobacco.
story1.p5: As for my mother... she was beyond extreme. A lawyer said things like, "If the statute of limitations had not passed, the abuse and related offenses alone could have meant ten years in prison without a suspended sentence," "Any judge would either explode or be stunned," and "The news would run with this for a week." She abandoned me twelve years ago. The fact that a lawyer went that far already says plenty.
story1.p6: The reason she abused me was, apparently, "because she tried to pass off her affair partner's child as my father's and failed." My younger sister and brother, who are that affair partner's children, were loved. I get along with them because they kept me from getting dragged into the abuse. Before I was thrown away, they helped me escape into homelessness and scraped together money for me out of their own allowances. They are excellent people. Also, unlike me, they are good-looking. Even if I escaped, without them she seemed likely to chase me down and kill me, so I mainly use a pen name. Even among friends, very few know my real name. For one thing, my name was originally supposed to be Yuna, and I changed it.
story1.p7: With a mother like that, the two grandmothers who had once gotten along went past hostility and both fell into despair. Oh, and my father died of a cerebral hemorrhage because of that dangerous woman. I think I was about one year old.
story1.p8: For two years, I drifted from friend's house to friend's house, was practically kept by female friends, and learned that mothers could be beings like this. I could only repay them by helping them study, though.
story1.p9: Homeless life was not as harsh back then, and around the university there were people who felt like highly educated homeless adults, so I wandered the area, still went to school, and somehow enjoyed it. I got pickles from McDonald's. I will never give that up. Then I learned my own birthday for the first time at city hall, traced my relatives, and ended up at the family story above. Once I became a middle school student, caregiving began. I secretly worked part-time jobs and later got taxed for it. In high school, I had ten hours of school, eight hours of part-time work, and two hours of housework, while the school demanded one hour of independent study per subject per day. My body suddenly stopped moving, but my two grandmothers kept making noise and I could not rest. Care facilities were not merely full; because problems kept happening, they would say they could not handle them, and we were passed around. I had to leave school early to tour facilities and so on, and I ended up with stress fractures in my legs. Apparently you can get stress fractures in your legs. Thinking back, getting a scooter or motorcycle license there would have changed a lot. I should have borrowed money and gone for it.
story1.p10: City hall was far away and kept sending me from place to place. In Aichi, factory work, especially Toyota-related work, fills the area, so psychiatry appointments were backed up for a month. Online consultations were not covered by insurance, and I had no money. Without the COVID period, I would definitely have been stuck. I wanted to study more. I wanted to play more too.
story1.p11: Personally, food service was enjoyable thanks to support programs. I remember thinking, "Oh, Lotteria is connected to Lotte," but the one near Toyota-shi Station was gone by the time I became a university student. I did gain weight, though.
story1.p12: There was another problem there: because I had been stingy with myself during homelessness and housework, I throw up if I eat anything a little expensive. Oil not agreeing with me is part of it, but because I had basically been starving myself, eating anything decent makes me sick. Beyond allergies, this also becomes a disadvantage in chemical-factory work. Compared with someone who could go into shock from nutrient-dense food, maybe I have it better. In that state, I started job hunting from my first year of university and went to several internships, but at a game company I was made to draw about forty standing character illustrations and one full illustration per day, and I simply came to hate drawing. On top of that, I cannot even list it as experience because the company itself disappeared. Nothing was released either. But if someone tried to claim IP over it the way they could with a vanished scenario, that would be a problem, so for works I made myself, I throw out just the first episode early and then leave them alone for a while. My main work is already in a state where I cannot use it anymore, though.
story1.p13: Today I originally wanted to write about plans and such, but I am not in any state to do that. I am just plainly exhausted, and because of debt I may have no choice but to renounce inheritance... Well, a lot happened, so I am resting today. I will post the unpublished works sooner rather than later.
story1.p14: I spent my youth ignoring almost everything except romance, so this time I want to play games and all sorts of things. Especially arcades. I did go on a school trip, but it was all Western-style places, so I want to try a hot spring inn too, like Ooedo Onsen Monogatari.
story1.p15: Not that I have managed to get a job yet.
story1.p16: Outside of game companies, the memorable one was real estate. A home-sales company suddenly disappeared, and when I went to the final interview, I was beaten badly by a customer who had not received their house after 20 million yen was taken from them. The police said they would pay my medical costs if I did not file a victim report, so I accepted, and then they did not pay. That drove me further into a fairly large debt. Including surgery, it was around 300,000 yen, I think. Well, there have been cases where they mistakenly restrained someone, so this was better than that.
story1.p17: There were cyberattacks and all kinds of other things too, but from there the caregiving worsened, inflation became painfully visible, and wages did not rise. The result was twelve hours of part-time work combined with classes. Even people making decent money at Toyota-related jobs were barely scraping by once caregiving costs were paid. Most of my part-time wages went to caregiving. I could no longer buy books, and my stress increased. More than anything, the damage from not being able to go to the hospital is now catching up with me.
story1.p18: Spending time consulting city hall costs me 5,000 yen in lost earnings. Hobbies are something I squeeze into spare five-minute gaps. The result is unemployment.
story1.p19: Ah, I at least wanted to be allowed to dream. I wanted a fun life. Recruiters are always dealing with overtime, I have no time to play, and none of my aptitudes line up.
story1.p20: As an additional thing to address these problems, here are the qualifications I plan to obtain. I simply do not have money, and before I could even take exams, my younger sister and brother immediately paid 800,000 yen, after insurance, for treatment of a bone bruise and stress fractures after caregiving ended, plus surgery for a meniscus injury. I need to adjust the household budget to reduce the damage from that.
story1.p21: In other conversations, many of the important factors are things other than qualifications, such as experience, values, and created works, or new areas where no qualification exists. Here, I am mainly deciding the qualification portion.

story2.chat2_p1: To roughly organize the text you uploaded, “Book-Reading Madness”: here are the tips for reading books easily (i.e., reading fast while keeping comprehension):
story2.chat2_p3: Use an eye patch or perforated glasses to halve eye strain. Reading with one eye at a time increases endurance. Remove the obi/covers: they can make pages slippery and harder to turn.
story2.chat2_p4: Adjust how you hold the book: on a desk, or hold it with your left hand and bend it, etc.—tune it based on how tired you are.
story2.chat2_p5:
Avoid heavy papers / “weapon-grade” books: there’s friction per page and your efficiency drops. Try them at the library first.
2. How to read
story2.chat2_p6: You can often understand a word from just its beginning and end → you don’t have to read every character.
story2.chat2_p7: → This can make your processing speed 2–4× faster.
story2.chat2_p8: Context completion: when something feels “off,” re-read only that part. Reading “carefully” can be counterproductive: instead of forcing yourself to feel satisfied on the spot, read once, then leave time and think later. Read multiple books in parallel: connections reinforce understanding and it sticks faster.
story2.chat2_p10: Pay attention to short-term memory + heart rate: keeping your pace steady makes it easier to organize memory. Break things up by chapter: even without sticky notes or bookmarks, you can remember where you were by feel.
story2.chat2_p11: Reading once and then giving it time before “accepting” it tends to be efficient for both understanding and memory.

story3.p1: Trigonometric Functions, or a Flat Sphere
story3.p2_rest: his time, I’m recording mainly a shift in mentality: positive, but not excessively positive—making compromises, while also not giving up.
story3.p3: From what doctors said, there were typical warning signs early on—things like falls at an age when I couldn’t even roll over in bed.
story3.p4: Whether it was because there was an affair partner and I wasn’t that partner’s child, I don’t know—but I’ve been told that while my siblings (with different fathers) were not abused, I was.
story3.p5: My father died around when I was one, from a stress-induced brain hemorrhage. That impacted the caregiving situation a lot.
story3.p6: → Around here I had a “blame others” tendency; I also don’t have memories, so I don’t dwell on it.
story3.p7: Violence: if I did anything other than music or studying, I’d be hit. With instruments—especially guitar—if it wasn’t liked, knives would come out. Drawing was also forbidden, so I wrote/drew on closet doors and sliding doors instead (thick-skinned).
story3.p8: → I followed instructions, but I didn’t feel affection in the first place, so emotionally it didn’t land. That said, I drew a clear line: I was strongly hostile toward violence and the like.
story3.p9: Diet: based on doctors’ assessment, it’s estimated that by around age four I didn’t have a normal diet. I survived on trash or food from other people’s houses. Oil-heavy food tended to cause indigestion, and the aftereffects lingered.
story3.p10: If an allergenic food made my throat swell and I didn’t eat it, there was violence. If it did swell, I couldn’t meet “singing quotas,” and I’d be choked.
story3.p11: → This later became one reason I mastered Italian cooking during caregiving. It improved blood-related issues too. Quietly huge.
story3.p12: Medication: I was pressured to “need to be a girl” and made to take things like the pill. In other cases there are stories of people taking the pill and developing female hormones and then dying by suicide, but in my case, that kind of stress/depression was relatively low.
story3.p13: → I didn’t match well with meds, so effects were limited; but my shoulder range of motion was slightly worse for heavy labor. I fixed that during university. I chose a university with a hospital on campus (also close by). I also leveraged cases/materials—for example, Koji Murofushi as an alumnus, who grew up in extreme poverty with a mother on welfare.
story3.p14: Sleep: if I slept in a bed, I’d be doused with cold water. So I slept on an outside bench, learned the time by body sense. If I opened a window or shutter to get outside, it would be closed as soon as I wasn’t watching. For the nightly checks to pour cold water, I had to not be in bed at 11 p.m. and 4 a.m.
story3.p15: There were many factories nearby, and they made noise at night, so staying awake wasn’t difficult.
story3.p16: → I became able to sleep anywhere and stopped caring about where I live. Not only did I become less prone to hypothermia—I started living in short sleeves year-round. Convenient since my “joke shirts” are short-sleeved.
story3.p17: In kindergarten my grades were half the average, which wasn’t “liked,” and it came back as violence. In elementary school I reached second in my grade, but I was pushed down because I wasn’t first.
story3.p18: → I can make peace with it: obsessing over grades doesn’t change anything. But I’ve basically never been praised; people either recoil or pity me, so I have no tolerance for praise. Simple.
story3.p19: In kindergarten my hearing aids were unusual and often stolen. Hearing aids affect not only volume but also balance (ear stones) that can cause vertigo, so they were essential.
story3.p20: → A left-right set was 140,000 yen; with insurance it drops by about 60,000. Too expensive for me to replace, so I recovered to the point I could go without. These days, if you reuse Bluetooth you can do it for 10,000 yen; in the extreme, I can build it in software or hardware, so it’s not that hard anymore.
story3.p21: I was remembered by other parents as “obedient and cute.” Some people later told me they compensated for that with extra care, or would test me even without teaching me. I learned things like piano, and they said things like my fingers were oddly shaped back then.
story3.p22: → This is when I learned morals and such. I studied whenever I wasn’t sleeping; I’d also slip out to places like hospitals around then.
story3.p23: My finger shape healed, but my hands stayed small—I recently lost a hand-size comparison with an elementary schooler. They’re so precisely small that in middle and high school there were basically no classmates who hadn’t touched them.
story3.p24: In elementary school I was moved because someone disliked that other parents evaluated me. The school was harsh to outsiders. I was bullied, but also ignored—so I’d just leave on my own. My test scores were high, so academically it wasn’t a concern.
story3.p25: Bullying and domestic violence can push some people toward depression/helplessness, and others toward aggression. But the individual differences are big, so it’s not something you can generalize for labeling others (like hiring profiles). In my case, I prioritized “disengage if it’s dangerous” over “endure,” and I chose to flee before damage happened.
story3.p26: In elementary school there was nothing to do at night, so I only studied. Spending less time at home made things easier and improved a lot. Around age ten my siblings both showed talent in music contests; my sister in particular later performed in an NHK program with about four people. Apparently she was top-class nationally.
story3.p27: → One reason my reading volume became abnormal: at hospitals I often became friends with kids my age in similar situations, and I survived by taking care of them in exchange for small food. Some kids had worse situations than me; at other kids’ homes I’d start thinking “I’m unhappy…” and then I stopped. (Another reason comes later.)
story3.p28: When I was bullied, I relied on girls; if teachers wouldn’t solve it, I’d make it a bigger deal by turning it into a boys-vs-girls conflict—things I couldn’t do against my mother.
story3.p29: Then I’d use it all: people would say they “helped me,” and I’d turn it into friendships or romantic relationships.
story3.p30: Bullying is often depicted in books, with accusations or revenge as common cases. I also skimmed things like “wouldn’t it be better to profit like you do in war?” and books about bullying theory; I collected fragments—like how verifying facts takes effort—and I had a strong tendency to see adversity as “earning time,” like: even if someone isn’t an ally, if they’re another enemy you can make them collide.
story3.p31: → Because I was bullied, I strengthened my relationships as described. After seeing other parents, I realized “that parent is abnormal!” I was late to friendships, but I gradually soaked in.
story3.p32: I assumed from the start that the bullying “event” wouldn’t be solved—but older people and the opposite sex have power.
story3.p33: Because of that, I was thrown away as “unneeded,” and for about two years from here I lived essentially homeless. It got easier; I gained friends; and within that, I learned for the first time how tragic my life actually was.
story3.p34: By then I’d read a lot. Seeing the background of Hemingway (famous even for the Nobel Prize in Literature)—a father who died by gun suicide, a mother who liked dressing him as a girl—I felt there were similarities, so it wasn’t like there were no cases. I also thought it was easier since there was no war.
story3.p35: → This period was fun because the environment wasn’t quite at the absolute limit, but I was sometimes sent back by child welfare or police, and my distrust of public institutions worsened a lot. (I also stopped going to hospitals for various reasons.)
story3.p36: After realizing how powerful friendships were, I basically lived at friends’ houses. My return from school refusal started around then; I simply visited the house of a girl I liked for months, got meals, and taught her as repayment.
story3.p37: → Middle and elementary schoolers can be somewhat closed-off, but in Aichi, except for places like Tokai High School, it’s mostly high-school entrance exams (“shiken” vs “juken,” apparently), so time disappears and it tends to be something only elementary schoolers do.
story3.p38: In high school, problems different from bullying arose due to the COVID period and such. The result was 16 cases resolved (excluding unresolved ones).
story3.p39: In those cases I didn’t over-involve myself; I warmed up slowly. Honestly, two-person time was better, so I didn’t intend to force “solutions.”
story3.p40: I didn’t “feel something” just because it was abuse; if anything, many stories are written in a tragic “I rose up” tone. So at that point I focused on extracting only facts, comparing, and reproducing—and I had already laid various plans.
story3.p41: Caregiving became complicated here. Because the situation had worsened badly, I rushed over after finding material about “abandonment by a person responsible for protection resulting in death.” Of course my mother didn’t come, so from middle school onward I handled things alone.
story3.p42: I had to watch two grandmothers. My grandfather did forestry and farming. The two grandmothers had Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s; they could move, but only enough for things like wandering at night. I sometimes escaped hospitals and got kicked out.
story3.p43: They both weighed around 80 kg. The weight gradually decreased, but I fractured bones several times. I was slender then; sometimes I was broken.
story3.p44: On top of dementia and the fact that my mother was basically someone who “killed” my father, my paternal grandmother was psychologically crushed: my father’s brother lost his wife, and my father told us not to get involved because the recruiting was intense; then two years after a near-cutoff, my father died.
story3.p45: My maternal grandmother, on top of that, had my mother’s sister and younger sister fleeing DV into her home; then the younger sister’s daughter also faced DV. While exhausted, she was further cornered by a situation where her daughter killed her husband.
story3.p46: I went back thinking it was a problem that wouldn’t have happened without me, but I didn’t know about the DV or bereavement—so it was good that I could act before it worsened.
story3.p47: → From here my tendency to blame others decreased. There had always been mutual misunderstandings with others, so I gradually adapted.
story3.p48: I still haven’t reached full psychological closure around here, but I regard the result as “not wrong.”
story3.p49: In high school, friends—especially female friends—were close with me. They helped me work through trauma. PTSD-like reflexive, instantaneous reactions happened occasionally, but they eased a lot. My positivity developed strongly here.
story3.p50: The “gyaru” group felt especially comfortable: even if you fought, the next day they were refreshed and clear. It calmed me.
story3.p51: I expanded variation in Italian desserts around this time.
story3.p52: Because it was during COVID, I mainly increased factory part-time work and friendships. I took the “two hours per subject per day of self-study” seriously; even while forcing my body, friendships were fun so I didn’t mind much. Resolving school refusal increased a lot here, and psychological check-ins among friends increased and improved things.
story3.p53: → However, factory part-time work had a strongly oppressive tendency even in a one-month stint: being made to sit on the ground all day, people disappearing during roll call, etc. I did it several times over about four years; there were a few deaths, and the supervisor was even referred to prosecutors. There were many “life danger” issues. Later research showed about 20 bullet points under “people who aren’t suited.” I kept drawing dangerous workplaces, and I stopped trusting temp agencies. Even if life was hard, I couldn’t afford to be hospitalized twice.
story3.p54: Here, self-blame around “solving things” weighed heavily and interfered with entrance exams. But I gave up on national/public universities because the faculty didn’t fit (Aichi Prefectural) or it was too difficult (Nagoya University). The places I’d originally decided on in middle school were far (Shinshu, Tokyo Metropolitan, Hiroshima), so I also gave those up. During exam season I judged that Russia’s invasion of Ukraine would raise prices even more than COVID, so I chose Chukyo University. (In the end that prediction was off, but each path had separate benefits, so I can’t say it was bad.)
story3.p55: My sister went to Toyota College of Technology and secretly supported me financially because she got a salary. My younger brother would flatter our mother, and in that gap my sister would support me—so they helped me in many ways, and I can’t thank them enough.
story3.p56: → Sort fundamental fixes and staged fixes; then “roughly align” them. Align them theoretically.
story3.p57: Both of them escaped from the house, so I’m relieved. If we gather in one place there’s a risk of being found, so for now we’ll live separately.
story3.p58: Sister/Brother → Because I took on the abuse for us
story3.p59: Me → Because my sister/brother looked away so they could free themselves from the abuse
story3.p60: That mutual relationship is why we’re close. All our fathers are different, and we won’t touch that in the future, but we check with each other so that genetic factors, abuse-triggered changes, or violent tendencies don’t surface.
story3.p61: From here, “real positivity” starts. For now I can accept things, but I think I’m still weak at turning it into benefit.
story3.p62: If anything, my friendships are strong, and I’ve raised myself to a level where I can live even with fewer part-time jobs. I had many “situations,” but not many “types,” so the experiences are somewhat monotonous—that’s the issue.
story3.p64: If I had to say, I have strong friendships and am able to make a living even with fewer part-time jobs. The problem is that although the number of places was large, the variety was small, so the experience was a bit monotonous.

story6.page_title: Reusing MV Direction with a Common IR | Akashi Isaka Archives
story6.title: Growing MV Direction from a Lightweight Environment
story6.p1_rest: hen you build MV direction, starting immediately inside heavy production environments like After Effects or Unity makes every revision expensive: every check and adjustment grows in scope. Lyric timing, position, color, motion, compositing order—if you keep redoing those small decisions close to the final pipeline, each failure becomes large.
story6.p2: So, use HTML/CSS/JavaScript as a lightweight preview environment. In the browser, validate lyrics, backgrounds, shapes, colors, transitions, glitches, zoom, shake, scroll sync, and audio sync first. The point is not to “finish the MV in HTML.” The point is to test direction in small pieces, have a human review and correct it, let AI organize it, then let a human decide again. That staged intervention lets you find failures early.
story6.p3: Once direction is decided, organize it as lyrics, timing, coordinates, color, opacity, effects, animation, asset references, layer order, easing, and keyframes. Save that as a common intermediate representation (IR), such as JSON. What you’re building is not “an MV made in HTML,” but design data for MV direction.
story6.p4: With a common IR, it becomes easier to deploy the same direction into different environments. In After Effects, use AE ExtendScript (JSX) to convert into Composition, Text Layer, Shape Layer, Footage, Marker, Keyframe, Expression, Effect, Pre-compose, and effect parameters. In Unity, load it in C# and connect it to Timeline, PlayableAsset, PlayableDirector, TextMeshPro, Canvas, RectTransform, Animator, Particle System, AudioSource, Addressables, and Prefabs. For WebGL, map it to Three.js, PixiJS, Canvas, WebGL shaders, textures, framebuffers, post effects, and GPU particles.
story6.p5: One thing to be careful about: After Effects does not read HTML/CSS/JavaScript like a browser. AE scripting doesn’t have a DOM renderer or a CSS layout engine. You must convert the direction you validated in HTML into AE-native layers, markers, keyframes, and effect settings. If you keep this vague, you end up talking about technically different things as if they were the same.
story6.p6: The value of this system is not “automating everything with AI.” It’s the opposite: keeping human judgment in place while enabling AI to intervene step by step. Instead of jumping straight into the final pipeline, you test in a lightweight environment, find mismatches, formalize them as direction data, and then move them to the required output target. That makes it less likely you’ll carry timing drift, coordinate drift, asset placement drift, or effect-order drift into later stages.
story6.p7: Running in a lightweight environment also matters for people. Even without a high-end PC or dedicated software, anyone who can run a browser can join prototyping and review. Because it’s less constrained by storage and specs, you can see—before entering the heavy production setup—who has timing sense, who can think about composition, and who is suited for asset organization. It becomes a useful entry point for scouting, prototyping, training, splitting roles, and operations.
story6.p8: In short, this isn’t a system for carelessly shortening work. Instead of rebuilding the same direction from scratch in AE, Unity, and WebGL every time, you use a common IR as the axis and organize the flow of review, revision, and deployment. Test in a light place, keep failures small, and hand off accurately to the environment you need. That’s the production workflow.

Power harassment, an atmosphere in which anything is tolerated as long as you can do your job, being forced to sit on the floor all day, no manual, panic when someone dies during an interview, and being told that if you withdraw during the interview you will be sued - the workplace goes beyond ``you'll be in trouble if you get in'' and mixes with the level of ``if you get in, you'll die''.
story4.p21: I can still endure the pain of not having money or being cornered. However, if you have a criminal record, your life is in danger, or your shoulder is damaged by sulfuric acid, the treatment costs will be negative even if you have the money. That's why it's impossible.
story4.p22: With this as a premise, the next step is to think about what I should observe, how I should preserve it, and how I should improve it.
story4.h2_2: Agriculture edition: “People” are not the only conditions for the field to work
story4.p23: The agricultural scene was relatively peaceful. Compared to the industrial environment, the atmosphere itself was quite calm.
story4.p24: Close to living things and nature. There is relatively little pressure on human relationships. There was even space to pick up an abandoned dog. The work itself was fun.
story4.p25: In particular, the sense of ``working as a broken human being'' was less felt than in industrial jobs.
story4.p26: →Although the physical strain was extremely heavy, I felt relatively peaceful mentally.

story4.h3_9: However, it is difficult for the industry
story4.p28: Fertilizer prices are rising. Current agriculture is extremely dependent on fertilizers. In particular, nitrogen fertilizer, fuel, and transportation costs are directly linked to the international situation.
story4.p29: Fertilizer procurement itself has become unstable due to Russia's suspension of exports and the worsening international situation.
story4.p30: →As a result, we are moving to a situation where ``the more we make, the more likely we are to be in the red.''
story4.p31: Mass-produced crops such as rice and wheat cannot rapidly raise unit prices. However, costs such as fertilizer, machinery, electricity, water management, and fuel continue to rise.
story4.p32: →Result: There are cases where the fertilizer costs alone result in a deficit.
story4.p33: Currently, there is even a reversal phenomenon in which ``it is easier to lose money by selling fertilizer instead of farming''.
story4.p34: Although income will decrease, it will be better in the end because you will be able to avoid the deficit caused by production. This is not just a recession, but a situation in which the act of production itself has become a liability.
story4.p35: If you sell the supplies you procured for production, you'll end up with a 30% loss, but if you grow them, you'll end up with a 50% loss, including the rising prices. These numbers are no joke, and the hunting association, which is working to prevent field vandalism, is cowed by the lawsuit, and the police are too rural to monitor it, so it's impossible. There are no benefits other than not starving to death.
story4.p36: Toyota City stopped purchasing wood several years ago. Forestry is a long-term industry, and was established based on the structure of growing trees, managing them, transporting them, and circulating them within the region.
story4.p37: →The continuity of forestry itself deteriorates due to the halting of regional circulation.
story4.p38: Both agriculture and forestry are approaching a state where they cannot be achieved by the region alone.
story4.h3_13: Collapse of rules of thumb due to climate change
story4.p39: Due to extreme temperatures in recent years, conventional rules of thumb no longer apply. Examples: Decrease in wasps, behavioral abnormalities in bees, pollination stagnation, ecosystem changes.
story4.p40: Bees in particular are not working properly, perhaps due to the heat, and pollination efficiency has decreased.
story4.p41: →We are now in a situation where the environment continues to change even if we accumulate agricultural knowledge.
story4.p42: High added value and branding actually increase dependence on overseas situations. Because the company relies on shipping, fuel, international markets, dining out, tourism, and exports, its business performance will be directly affected by the deterioration of the situation in the Middle East.
story4.p43: → “High added value = stability” is no longer the case.
story4.p44: It's not a case of "lack of effort," but rather, "dependence on the external environment has reached its limit."
story4.p45: The agricultural field itself was relatively peaceful, and there was room for people to work like humans. However, in reality, we are too dependent on the international situation, fertilizers, climate change, fuel, shipping, and the collapse of regional circulation, making it difficult to maintain with on-site efforts alone.
story4.h3_16: Problems seen in the IT/media field
story4.p46: Among IT companies, we have confirmed that multiple organizations have actually been victims of cyberattacks.
story4.p47: One company restricted disclosure to shareholders and customers, and went so far as to pay a ransom. At the other company, an advance proposal was rejected on the grounds that it was too costly, and profits subsequently fell significantly.
story4.p48: Even back then, I feel that given the international situation since the invasion of Ukraine, the increase in Russian attacks, attacks on American security companies, and supply chain risks were fully predictable.
story4.p49: However, in reality, short-term costs were prioritized, security was ignored, and judgments that ``it's okay for now'' were given priority, and problems emerged as a result.
story4.p50: →For that reason, I decided that it would be better for me to leave than to remain in an organization that has entered the stage of rebuilding itself after a problem has occurred.
story4.h3_17: Publisher edition: Industry with the best psychological compatibility
story4.p51: Of all the industries I've worked in, being a publisher was the most fun I've had. "Knowledge and conversation" were strongly connected, including behind-the-scenes stories, insights, small talk, human relationships, industry history, and shared context.
story4.p52: Unlike the industrial industry, which is all about numbers, management, safety margins, and personal exhaustion, there was a strong sense that this was an industry that dealt with people themselves.
story4.p53: Publishers were the exact opposite of the "official honesty" of civil servants, and were strongly influenced by obligations, personal connections, atmosphere, power, and tacit understanding.
story4.p54: At times, there were also quite dangerous aspects, such as concealing crimes, maintaining relationships, and coordinating within the industry.
story4.p55: However, on the contrary, he found the ``raw human society'' itself interesting. Because he had seen how agriculture-related areas and governments were being treated sloppily, he had the tolerance and understanding that ``a world cannot be run by just being pretty'' and was psychologically compatible with him.
story4.p56: Particularly acclaimed was a document that organized and analyzed the founding, history, books, number of volumes, genealogy, etc. of a certain publishing company.
story4.p57: →I was evaluated not just for my impressions, but for my ability to put together history and structure.
story4.h3_20: However, I also felt that my ability was lacking.
story4.p58: In the interview, I had a strong feeling that I was simply not good enough.
story4.p59: In addition, the industry as a whole was increasing the number of science-minded human resources, which were already large, due to the demand for AI development, data processing, analysis, translation, overseas support, anti-piracy technology, and legal affairs. In addition, the number of foreign human resources is increasing due to demand for translation and responding to overseas markets.
story4.p60: →As a result, the competitive environment itself was changing.
story4.p61: This is not a ``dream industry,'' but an ``industry where knowledge, connections, analysis, and human relationships are intricately intertwined.''
story4.p62: Publishing was not just a creative job; it was a world that involved organizing information, understanding the atmosphere, history, personal connections, markets, and power all at the same time.
story4.p63: →I had a strong impression that this industry was in a different direction from industry and agriculture, and that it was an industry that was like a miniature version of society itself.
story4.h3_22: Game company edition: A different atmosphere than that of a publisher
story4.p64: I also got involved with a game company, but I didn't feel like there was as much compatibility with them as with a publisher. Rather than human relationships, small talk, shared context, and a culture of reflection, the focus was on production speed, fluidity, external collaboration, and amount of work, and the atmosphere itself was quite different.
story4.p65: It was an environment where I was forced to draw a lot. However, at the time, his arm was severely damaged due to industrial work, which placed a heavy physical burden on him.
story4.p66: →Rather than a pure contest of production ability, I had a strong impression that it was a ``production environment based on wear and tear''.
story4.p67: On the other hand, their ability to organize materials was highly evaluated. Responsible for recruitment, information organization, classification, management, etc.
story4.p68: →The ability to organize and structure information was used, rather than simple drawing.
story4.p69: Game companies had many connections with other companies, and their structure was quite fluid. There were many outsourced, subcontractor, contract, freelance, and temporary employees, and the ratio of full-time employees was low.
story4.p70: →I got the impression that it was more like a "constantly changing production network" than a "company".
story4.p71: I also felt that communication was unstable. There is a lack of information sharing, a lack of management, a weak legal sense, a difference in compliance awareness, and an ambiguous sense of intellectual property.
story4.p72: →I now understand why Nintendo is so strict about intellectual property and compliance.
story4.h3_27: Creative structure that takes advantage of isolation
story4.p73: I was impressed by the structure of the work, which draws out the creative abilities of the creator while maintaining a state of isolation. Due to the closed environment, strong dependence on production, fluid human relationships, and expendable production, an atmosphere existed in which creators maximized their output.
story4.p74: →However, I also felt that it was ethically dangerous.
story4.h3_28: Structure comparison: publishers and game companies
story4.p75: Publishing companies are built on close human relationships and long-term relationships. Editing, writing, printing, sales, agency, industry connections, etc. all overlap over the long term.
story4.p76: →The structure is similar to "addition of integers" (accumulation of small pluses and minuses, long-term relationships are a buffer, and past assets accumulate).
story4.p77: However, sometimes "multiplication" is mixed in, such as big artists, powerful people, large IPs, brokers, and distributors. It's usually stable, but sometimes huge factors cause the whole thing to fluctuate.
story4.p78: On the game company side, there is a high level of fluidity with outsourcing, contracts, freelance work, one-off projects, short-term teams, etc.
story4.p79: →The structure is similar to "multiplication including decimal numbers" (it gradually attenuates like 0.9 x 0.8 x 0.95 x 1.1...).
story4.p80: Negative factors such as legal problems, breakdowns in outsourcing, breakdowns in communication, lack of management, and delays in production have a huge impact on the entire business, making it difficult for publishers to absorb them based on human nature and accumulation.
story4.p81: →As a result, there is a feeling of ``gradually chipping away toward completion''.
story4.p82: The biggest conclusion I got from my part-time jobs and internships was that ``systems that can be reproduced'' are stronger than ``effort.''
story4.p83: So from now on, rather than trying my best to do it haphazardly, I will separate the steps, record them, and put them into a form that can be passed on. I'm going to be on the side of designing things that will turn the workplace around.

story5.p1_rest: ou can write "I like being a VTuber" or "I want to be involved in content" as your reason for applying. However, if that's all there is to it, it's a bit off from the core of why I'm aiming for Brave group. What I have seen is not only the projects and videos that appear on the surface, but also how information flows behind the scenes, where it gets stuck, and how it can be passed on to the next person.
story5.p2: I spent a lot of time ``preserving information'' before creating works. At a time when my life was falling apart, my plans for the future often fell apart. Therefore, before talking about dreams and efforts, it was first necessary to create a preservation format that would not collapse even in the face of bankruptcy. Leave a log. Find structure. Create a format that can be restored later. This was not a hobby, but a very serious life skill.
story5.p3: The reason why I created the VTuber archive is also rooted in this. It is not an extension of pushing activities, but rather observation and preservation of the structure. The number of talents will increase. Attributes increase. Offices will increase. Distribution, videos, events, goods, music, overseas expansion and other media will increase. Each time, the amount of information increases, but the increase in information does not necessarily make it easier to understand. Rather, without classification and guidance, the amount of information itself becomes noise.
story5.p4: →The essence of archiving work was not input but specification. The main focus was on creating a format that others could read, search, compare, and modify later.
story5.p5: The important point here is that it is not enough for the information to be "correct." Even if you have accurate data, you can't use it if you don't know where it's stored. You can't search if you don't have all the terms. If you don't know who updated it, it will become outdated. If authority is ambiguous, disclosure accidents will occur. If you don't know who made the decision to provide the information, you won't be able to go back to the cause when a problem occurs.
story5.p6: Therefore, the work of handling information does not end with just "gathering" it. It can be used in the field for the first time, including naming, classification, version management, guidance, scope of publication, update responsibility, checkpoints, and handover format. Compression of the UI and text is part of this, and is intended to reduce the burden on the reader and shorten the distance it takes to make a decision.
story5.p7: This is why we aim to become a Brave group. In organizations with multiple businesses, multiple IPs, multiple talent, and multiple content formats running simultaneously, the flow of information is bound to become clogged. This isn't because anyone is lazy. This is because as the organization grows, the production sites become more divided, and the number of countries, languages, and production companies increases, the number of invisible specifications increases.
story5.p8: Invisible specifications include, for example, ``Who should go through this confirmation?'' ``To what extent can this material be used?'' ``Which version is the latest version?'' ``What is the scope of what can be shown outside the company?'' ``Are overseas judgment standards the same as domestic ones?'' ``Are the granularity of rights confirmation for distribution, music, and events consistent?'' The more things like this increase without being clearly stated, the more it becomes impossible to stop them with the attention of individuals.
story5.p9: Fixed point observation from the Unlimited era and the current Buspo! Looking at the multifaceted group structure including , RIOT MUSIC, ENILIS, etc., modern virtual content management suffers from multiplicative attenuation due to fluid production networks. One failure to communicate leads to another failure to confirm. A single change in naming can lead to unsearchable results. A single difference in authority can lead to discrepancies in public decisions. Small frictions multiply, leading to delays in production, rework, flameouts, and loss of trust.
story5.p10: In particular, with the current structure expanding not only domestically but also to Thailand, South Korea, and the United States, differences in rules from site to site directly lead to distortions in internal control. Given the differences in language, business practices, legal acumen, fan culture, disclosure standards, and compliance awareness, there are limits to just being careful, reading the atmosphere, and doing your best. In fact, the more an organization has passed the period when it can be driven by spirit, the more accidents will occur if the organization relies on spirit.
story5.p11: →The problem is not a lack of good intentions among people, but rather that the structure is such that even people with good intentions can get away with it. Therefore, we need to stop with design, not with psychology.
story5.p12: What I want to do with Brave group is not to reduce the energy in the workplace. In fact, it's the opposite, and it's about not letting your energy get sucked into unnecessary checking, searching for things, reworking, and personal memories. We will prepare behind-the-scenes specifications so that creators and talents can concentrate on their expression.
story5.p13: This is no fancy job. However, the more complex the organization, the more effective it is. Materials are not scattered. Judgments do not become personal. Updates don't stop. It won't break due to handover. When a problem occurs, you can go back to what specifications were stuck, rather than someone's guts. This is not to blame you for your failures, but to help you get back on track so you don't make the same mistakes next time.
story5.p14: On the other hand, I also want to improve and strengthen my skills, and even though I live an unstable life due to my environment, I am mentally stable due to the cooperation of many people, so I would not lose anything no matter where I am placed.
story5.p15: I have heard many times in the field that there is a lack of effort and perseverance. However, the reality was the opposite. I'm making an effort. He also has guts. The problem was that operation, which required effort and perseverance, was a losing design from the beginning. Rather than increasing the number of people who work hard, it is better to create systems that make it difficult for people to quit even if they don't work hard, and it will last longer.
story5.p16: What I can present is not just my subjective opinion as a creator. These are logs and techniques for observing, disassembling, converting to specifications, and continuing to update. I would like to connect the "power to leave" that I have cultivated through archives and the "power to reach" that I have cultivated through writing, UI, and leads to a design that will stop the decay of the organization.
story5.p17: The Brave group environment is supposed to be complex, busy, and with little space. That's why observation, organization, and operational design are so effective. I don't want to simplify the complexity and crush it, but I want to make it into a form that can be handled as it is. Even if multiple IPs, multiple countries, and multiple sites are running at the same time, information will not get clogged, decisions will not disappear, and it will continue even if someone leaves. To that end, we would like to deploy the logs and technology we have developed so far to each site of Brave group Co., Ltd.
